Note 3 -

Details of shareholding under the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) category:
The classification of shareholding under the FDI category for the purpose of this shareholding pattern is as per FAQ No. 6 of NSE Circular dated June 30, 2022, which defines FDI to mean as defined under Rule 2(r) of FEM (NDI) Rules, 2019. As per Rule 2(r) of FEM (NDI) Rules, 2019, (a) Foreign Direct Investment means investment through equity instruments by a person resident outside India in an unlisted Indian company or (b) in ten per cent or more of the post issue paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis of a listed Indian company.
Further, as per FAQ No. 2 of NSE Circular dated June 30, 2022, the categorization and disclosure of shareholders falling under multiple categories should be considered and disclosed under the category falling first in order prescribed in the shareholding format under Table III, in order to avoid duplication of same shareholders in multiple category(ies). Under the broader category of Institutions (Foreign), the first sub-category is that of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), followed by other sub-categories such as FPI category I, FPI category II, etc.
In order to comply with both the aforesaid FAQs, all the Institutional shareholders falling within the definition of FDI as per Rule 2(r) of FEM (NDI) Rules, 2019, are now grouped under the sub-category of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) under the category Institutions (Foreign). The total shares held by the shareholders grouped under FDI category are 11,66,57,926 shares (representing 28.60% of the total share capital).
Further, we wish to submit that shares qualifying for FDI as per Rule 2(r) of FEM (NDI) Rules, 2019, are 9,63,29,299 shares (representing 23.62% of the total share capital) and the balance shares 2,03,28,627 (representing 4.98% of the total share capital) do not qualify as FDI as per as per Rule 2(r) of FEM (NDI) Rules, 2019, but are categorised as FDI due to FAQ No. 2 of NSE Circular dated September 30, 2022. (i) Certain Individual shareholders holding shares are qualifying under FDI as per past submission to RBI are categorised under Non-Resident Indian(s) (“NRIs”) category; (ii) Certain Residential individual shareholders who were reported as FDI in the past RBI submission(s) are Public shareholder(s) categorized as “Resident Individuals holding nominal share capital up to Rs. 2 lakhs”.

Note 7:

Details of computation of foreign ownership limits under Table IV:
For the purpose of computing the foreign ownership limits in Table IV, up to the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the Company had included the holdings of Non-Resident Indians (non-repatriable basis). With effect from the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and in line Rule 2(s) of FEM (NDI) Rules, 2019, which does not consider investment by Non-Resident Indians (non-repatriable basis) as ‘foreign investment’, the Company has not considered the same for computing the foreign ownership limits.
